title: How to Colour a CNC Relief Carving So It Still Looks Like Wood
excerpt: The tinted-wash method behind the coloured carvings on this site, stage by stage on one cardinal panel: sealing, mixing thin washes from artists' acrylics, laying the first colour, shading, keeping the ground clean, the glaze that ties it all together, and the matte topcoat. seo_title: How to Color a CNC Relief Carving: Tinted Washes, Step by Step
seo_description: How to paint a CNC relief carving so the wood grain still shows: seal, thin artists' acrylics into washes, colour the subject, shade, glaze the recesses and seal with a matte topcoat. Brands, colour recipes and troubleshooting.

email.subject: How to colour a relief carving without hiding the wood
email.intro:
A reader asked how the coloured carvings on the site are done, whether it is paint or stain, and how to do it on their own cuts. It is neither, quite. It is thin translucent washes over sealed wood, then the same dark glaze that makes any relief read.

The new guide walks the whole method on one cardinal panel, stage by stage: what to buy, how thin to mix, where the colour goes and where it must not, and the two steps that turn craft-paint brightness into something that looks like it grew there.
